findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Observed that the ventilation hood lights are out and need replaced. PIC was notified and will get the light bulbs replaced before the next routine cleaning. Ensure that the light intensity where food employees are working is sufficiently bright enough to work with potentially dangerous equipment.
findings.citation_text: 6-303.11(C) Intensity. The light intensity shall be: (C) At least 540 lux (50 foot candles) at a surface where a FOOD EMPLOYEE is working with FOOD or working with UTENSILS or EQUIPMENT such as knives, slicers, grinders, or saws where EMPLOYEE safety is a factor. [C]

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Observed that the PIC’s Allergen Awareness Training certificate has expired. PIC was notified and plans to renew certificates by the next routine inspection, and possibly have other staff members certified. Ensure that all CFPMs have training in basic allergen awareness principles.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed three canned goods with significant dents near the top/bottom of the can. CORRECTED: Discussed with PIC checking cans for visible dents and which areas of the can to check, and the PIC excluded the cans from service. Ensure that canned foods are in good condition and not exposed to potential contamination, in this case the damage to the inner lining from dents at the top, bottom, or side seam.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed no measurable concentration of Chlorine in the the sanitizer bucket. CORRECTED: Discussed with PIC, the sanitizer bucket was remade, and observed a concentration of 50pm. Ensure that sanitizing solutions are measuring at effective concentrations - 50-200pm.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION: Inspectors observed that the scoop inside the salt bin does not have a handle. Scoops for ready-to-eat foods must have handles that are stored above the top of food to avoid contamination. Ensure that the salt bin has a scoop with a handle by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed several personal items, like sweaters, hanging above food service items in the dry storage areas. CORRECTED: PIC was notified, and the items were moved to a designated area that is away from food service items. Ensure that personal items are kept separate from food service areas and food content surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.110 Using Dressing Rooms and Lockers. (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
THIS IS A THIRD REPEAT VIOLATION: Inspectors observed that not all employees have completed the food handler training. The PIC was educated that all employees who do not have a CFPM (Certified Food Protection Manager) certificate must have food handler certificates. Ensure that all required employees complete the food handler training and copies of the certificates are kept at the facility by the next routine inspection. Inspector will return on Monday, 1 June 2026 to check that staff have Food Handler certificates.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The employee was educated about the proper hand washing procedure when the action was observed. Ensure that employees always use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed a pizza pan and cutting board stored behind the faucet of the triple sink. The PIC was educated that food contact surfaces can become contaminated by water splashes, food residue, or other debris stored in this position. After education the PIC moved the pizza pan and cutting board into a new location. Ensure that food contact surfaces are always stored in a position that allows them to remain clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed several foods in the pizza prep cooler without proper date marking. The PIC stated the pizza sauce, sausage, green peppers, onions, and olives have been in the prep cooler since Sunday. The rest of the foods were prepared today. The necessary foods were date marked during the inspection. Foods that remain at the facility longer than 24 hours must be date marked to indicate the 7-day maximum. Ensure the facility follows the proper date marking procedure. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf).

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed that not all employees have completed the food handler training. There was at least one employee who had an expired certificate. Ensure that all employees complete the food handler training. 

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed mops stored in the back room to be stored on the floor. Mops must be stored in a manner which does not pose a risk of contamination and facilitates air drying. Ensure that mops are stored either in the top portion of the mop bucket or are stored hanging inverted along the wall. 

6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOALTION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION(S)

Facility has several repeat and/or priority/priority foundation violations. The person-in-charge is responsible for ensuring that no priority/priority foundation violations are occurring within the facility. Further, person-in-charge is responsible for ensuring that proper corrective actions are taken and maintained to prevent continued violations. As such, a follow-up is issued for 10/26/2023 to ensure compliance with all priority/priority foundation violations and the correction of repeat violations. 

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
The hand sink in the kitchen was not stocked with hand soap. Ensure that hand washing sinks are properly stocked with hand soap and paper towels at all times and that hand washing is occurring often. A follow-up is issued for 10/05/2023.

6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a can with a severe dent along the upper seam stocked in with the rest of the cans. Ensure that cans are checked and if the integrity of the cans cannot be guaranteed, refuse delivery of the product. Inspector will return on 10/05/2023 to check cans for damage at that time. 

3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION(S)

No sanitizer solution was prepared during the inspection while active food preparation was occurring. Ensure that multiple sanitizer buckets are prepared at the start of the shift and that sanitizer is maintained at proper concentration during all hours of operation when active food preparation/service is occurring. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that the can opener blade in the kitchen had a significant amount of dried food residue on it. The blade of the can opener is a food-contact surface and as such must be cleaned daily or anytime contamination has occurred. Ensure that all food-contact surfaces are cleaned and sanitized as required.

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION.

Facility is utilizing crockpots to reheat/cook white sauces. Operator has purchased a broiler to reheat the sauces properly but has not been using it for reheating. Ensure that all foods are reheated/cooked appropriately. A follow-up is issued for 10/02/2023 to ensure that reheating/cooking is occurring properly.

3-403.11: (A) TCS FOOD cooked, cooled, and reheated shall be reheated to 165F for 15 seconds. (P) (B) If reheated with microwave, FOOD rotated, stirred, covered, and allowed to stand for 2 minutes covered. (P) (C) Commercially processed FOOD shall be reheated to 135F. (P) (D) Reheating may not exceed 2 hours.(P) (E) Unsliced portions of MEAT roasts may be reheated according to oven parameters and minimum TCS conditions. (C)

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Several items throughout the facility are missing proper date marking. Items observed without date marking include mushrooms, diced peppers, diced onions and meat sauce. Per conversation with person-in-charge, these items are used rapidly but often exceed the 24 hour requirement for date marking. Ensure that all prepared items being stored in the coolers/freezers (including items removed from cans) are date marked as required with either the date prepared/opened or the 7-day discard date. A follow-up is issued for 10/05/2023 to ensure compliance with date marking requirements.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION(S)

Inspector observed a wet wiping cloth on the counter near the stovetop. Wiping cloths, if wet, must be stored in sanitizer solution between uses and may never be stored sitting on countertops. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are stored in sanitizer solution at all times when not actively being used to wipe surfaces.

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Several heavily used sponges are located in the warewashing area and sitting on the triple sink where dishes are being cleaned. Sponges are not appropriate for cleaning food-contact surfaces. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are cleaned with wiping cloths or other sanitary cleaning methods.

4-101.16: Sponges may not be used in contact with cleaned and SANITIZED or in-use FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION(S)

Ice accumulation is observed on all surfaces of the white upright freezer in the kitchen. The seal around the edge of the freezer is damaged allowing rapid entry and freezing of condensation within the freezer. Operator states that the freezer will be replaced. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION(S)

Inspector observed x2 mops which were stored on the floor in front of the mop sink/bucket in the back warewashing/storage area. Mops must be stored in the top portion of the mop bucket or hanging inverted along a wall to prevent contamination. Ensure that mops are stored properly at all times. 

6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Upon completion of the inspection today, facility has several priority and repeat violations which have not been corrected. Person-in-charge is responsible for ensuring compliance with Food Code requirements. The facility must ensure that ALL priority violations and repeat violations are corrected and remain corrected at all times of operation. A 30-day follow-up is being issued to ensure compliance. Inspector will return on 4/17/2023 to evaluate the operations of the facility in their entirety.

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Inspector observed improper hand washing procedure and changing of gloves without hand washing between activities. An employee washed hands for less than 20 seconds and without using a barrier (paper towel) to turn off the faucet. This violation was observed during the previous routine inspection and is a repeat violation. A follow-up is issued for Monday 03/20/2023. Ensure that prior to that date all staff have been instructed on proper hand washing procedure that that the person-in-charge enforces proper hand washing expectations at all times. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
No sanitizer buckets or sanitizer spray was available upon entry to the facility where food preparation was occurring. Sanitizer must be available in all areas of the facility where active food preparation and cleaning is occurring. A follow-up is issued for Monday 03/20/2023. Ensure that staff is preparing sanitizer solution daily (or as needed with spray if using paper towels) and that sanitizer is available where employees are working with food. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper cooking time and temperatures
findings.comment:
A white sauce was observed cooking in a crock pot on the countertop in the southwest corner of the kitchen. A crock pot is not a proper piece of equipment heating/reheating food as it does not heat rapidly and allows foods to remain outsid critical limits for extended periods of time during food preparation. Foods must be cooked/reheated on a stovetop and may be hot held at 135 degrees in a crock pot AFTER heating to 165 degrees. A follow-up is being issued for 03/20/2023 to ensure the facility is following proper cooking procedures including times, temperatures and equipment. 

3-401.11: (A) Heat all parts of food to: 1) 145F for 15 seconds (raw eggs for immediate service, fish and intact meats); 2) 155F for 17 seconds (injected meats, raw eggs, and comminuted meats); 3) 165F for <1 second (poultry, stuffed meats/pastas/stuffing). (P)  (B) Whole roasts should follow cooking log (P) and have oven preheated (Pf).  (C) Undercooked if 1) NOT HSP; 2) whole, intact beef; 3) steak top and bottom cooked to 145F (C).  (D) Any raw foods if 1) NOT HSP (C), 2) not comminuted to kids (Pf), 3) Consumer Advisory, 4) Variance with HACCP plan approved (C).

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Wet wiping cloths may not be left sitting out and must be stored between uses in sanitizer solution. No sanitizer solution was made on arrival however wiping clothes were observed to be in use. Further, wiping cloths which were previously wet are observed to be dry and crusted hanging in the back area on the bracket of a shelf across from the triple sink. Ensure that wet wiping cloths which are no longer in use are laundered properly and that these wiping cloths, when being used in the facility, are stored between active wiping in an approved sanitizer solution. This is a repeat violation from previous inspection.

4-901.12: Wiping cloths laundered in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT without mechanical dryer shall be air-dried in location and manner that prevents contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES. Wiping cloths may be stored in sanitizer solution after laundering.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Clean utensils are observed to be stored in a plastic container on shelves along the west wall of the facility. Trays on which food is served are also stored on these shelves. Inspector observed a pack of cigarettes, a lighter, and a used glove sitting on top of a the stack of trays on these shelves. These items come in contact with food which allows for potential contamination. Items which are potential sources of contamination may not be stored on top of or next to these items at any time. Ensure that ALL sources of contamination are separated from foods and food contact surfaces. Correct by the next routine inspection. 

4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
During the previous inspection, inspector observed a large amount of ice accumulation in the white upright freezer in the kitchen. Upon inspection today, there continues to be a large amount of accumulated ice. This is a repeat violation. Ensure that the ice is scraped/defrosted at a frequency that prevents the accumulation of ice in the freezer and ensure that all seals are tight fitting to prevent condensation from occurring within the freezer.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector oberved the following areas of the facility to be in disrepair and in need of sealing/repair/replacement to ensure that surfaces in areas subject to food and moisture are smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable:
- the hand sink in the kithen has missing/deteriorated caulking along the back edge
- the triple sink in the back room has molded and peeling caulking along the back edge
- the area of wall directly above the base coving to the right of the triple sink is peeling and needs to be repainted or otherwise sealed
- the base coving and wall panels along both interior doorways at the rear of the facility are peeling back leaving surfaces behind them exposed to food/water and other debris
- tile in the kitchen in front of the pizza oven is cracked
- tile in the back room in front of the rear door and in the southwest corner is cracked

Ensure that these surfaces are brought into compliance by creating surfaces which are smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable by re-caulking/sealing, painting, replacing and/or repairing these items. 

This is a repeat violation from the previous inspection.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed mops stored in the back room to be stored on the floor. Mops must be stored in a manner which does not pose a risk of contamination and facilitates air drying. Ensure that mops are stored either in the top portion of the mop bucket or are stored hanging inverted along the wall. 

6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed personal drinks stored in the dry storage area and a personal phone resting on a countertop in the kitchen where food preparation is occurring. Ensure that there is a designated area for personal items away from food and food preparation activities and that staff are aware and comply with the requirement to keep personal items in such a location. 

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
Person-in-charge is requird to have allergen training completed. During the previous inspection, person-in-charge did not have the proper certification. During the inspection today, allergen training has not been completed. Ensure that this training is completed by the next routine inspection. This is a repeat violation. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed hand washing performed twice without a barrier and for less than 20 seconds. Discussed with PIC and PIC discussed with staff. Ensure hand washing is done for at least 20 SECONDS and with a BARRIER. Educated staff immediately. Corrected on site. Ensure that hand washing continues regularly throughout operations and with proper procedure.

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Inspector observed wiping cloths which were moist sitting on the countertop in the middle of the room (with the can opener). Wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizer when not in use. Ensure that wiping cloths are stored appropriately.

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
The sugar scoop handle was observed sitting in the sugar itself. Handles must be stored upright. Ensure that the handles of utensils stored in food are not in contact with the food.

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Ice is accumulating in the white upright freezer and in the white chest freezer in back. This poses a risk of contamination to food in the freezer. Ensure that ice is removed often enough to prevent such accumulations.

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The following areas have missing/deteriorating caulking and must be re-caulked to ensure a smooth, nonabsorbent and easily cleanable surface:
- Around hand sink
- Around triple sink

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
Person-in-charge allergen certification is expired. Allergen certification is required in high-risk facilities. Ensure that person-in-charge has valid allergen certification. This is a repeat violation. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
Person in charge has an expired CFM certificate. Ensure that person in charge has a valid, non-expired certificate during all operations. This is a repeat from previous inspection. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Several wiping cloths were observed throughout the facility. Wet cloths were observed on counter tops and hanging on the sink. Wet wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizer solution when not in use. Hanging wet wiping cloths on the hand sink is not an option. If a rag is being allowed to air dry, hang with the remainder of the rags waiting to be laundered. Store all wet rags in sanitizer solution to prevent harmful microbial growth and contamination of surfaces being sanitized. This is a repeat violation from previous inspection. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Clean pizza peels were observed to be sitting on top of a soiled wire rack and on top of soiled cardboard. If cardboard is being used to put underneath utensils, ensure that it is switched out every time that it becomes soiled. The wire rack must be cleaned regularly as well. Keep all surfaces that cleaned and sanitized utensils are sitting on clean to sight and touch to prevent contamination. Pizza peels were removed from these areas by the operator. Corrected on site. 

4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Two of the lower counters in the facility had a thick layer of debris on them. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned regularly to prevent the buildup of dust and other debris. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The hood over the pizza oven and stove is covered in a large amount of black dust and oil. Have a hood cleaning service visit to clean the hood. Operator stated he has called and is scheduling a time to have the hood cleaned and maintained after noticing some of this dust drop from the hood recently. 

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Several food handler certificates have expired as of the time of this inspection. Ensure that all food-handling employees are certified food handlers when working in the facility. 

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
Operator’s allergen awareness certificate is expired as of the date of this inspection. Ensure that allergen awareness training is completed and the certificate renewed. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

Observed no CFPM licensed at the facility. PIC was a CFPM and has not re-taken the course. Provided information regarding how to take the exam with a registered proctor in the general comments. See general comments page. PIC has taken the course online; however, has not taken the exam. Ensure exam is completed before next routine inspection, licensure completed, and copy of license available in the public health folder. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed multiple employees to wash hands incorrectly throughout the inspection. Discussed with PIC and employees. A barrier such as a paper towel should be used to turn off the faucets. Ensure proper hand washing technique and that staff is aware. COS.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-302.12: (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets. 

Observed no probe thermometer at the facility. Probe thermometer is necessary to accurately check internal temperatures of food items. Discussed with PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 4/7/22.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

Observed no test strips for the bleach. PIC indicated facility had test strips, but the item has become lost. Ensure test strips are available to check bleach concentration - 50 to 200 ppm. Discussed with PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 4/7/22.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools. 

Observed a mop bucket with dirty mop water near the mop sink. Upon discussion with PIC, PIC indicated the mop water was left from Sunday night (2 days ago). Ensure staff is aware to dump mop water nightly in the mop sink and not let stay stagnant in the mop bucket. COS.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Employee observed using handwashing sink to fill a container of water to be used for food preparations. Upon arrival, inspector found cans of olives and mushrooms draining in the basin of the handwashing sink. CORRECTED-- Provided education. Keep handwashing sinks clear and use them only for handwashing.
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: The following items in the top of the pizza prep cooler were observed to be out of temperature: pizza sauce 47F; ground beef 50F; ham 47F.CORRECTED-- Since PIC stated that all foods had been in the cooler overnight (none had been prepped this evening), all out of temperature foods from the top of the pizza prep cooler were voluntarily discarded. See general comments for additional notes.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]
